s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction with highly vascularized mass
salient_findings: Voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
Hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Considerable uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy regarding rib and vertebral lesions
key_facts: Woman in her 30s with no relevant medical history
Endoscopic examination found a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
MRI confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Radioiodine scintigraphy found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
Sinonasal tumor had low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy
Serum thyroglobulin was significantly elevated at 4432 ng/mL
Biopsy results confirmed VTC metastasis in both costal and sinonasal tumor biopsies

raw.champion: Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma with Vertebral and Costal Metastases
raw.rationale: The patient's significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin, the presence of a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity with low iodine uptake, and biopsy results confirming VTC metastasis in both costal and sinonasal tumor biopsies support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Follicular Thyroid Carcinoma with Distant Metastasis
rejected.why: The biopsy results specifically pointed to VTC metastasis, not follicular thyroid carcinoma.

rejected.label: Hürthle Cell Carcinoma with Vertebral Metastasis
rejected.why: There is no specific indication of Hürthle cell carcinoma in the biopsy results or other diagnostic findings.

rejected.label: Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma with Skull Base Invasion
rejected.why: The diagnostic findings, including the significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin and biopsy results, do not specifically support medullary thyroid carcinoma.

rejected.label: Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma with Aggressive Metastasis
rejected.why: The described progression and findings do not indicate the highly aggressive nature typical of anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.
